title: Statistical Sampling and Data Presentation
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Sampling and Data Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use the terms population and sample; sampling techniques (simple random, stratified, systematic, quota, opportunity); calculate and interpret measures of location and variation, including standard deviation; coding.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on statistics: sampling methods, stratified samples, mean and standard deviation from lists, sums and grouped data, and coding. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Adding a constant changes the mean, not the standard deviation.
body_html:
How it works

A sample is part of the population. Random methods: simple random, systematic, stratified. Non-random: quota, opportunity.

Variance σ² = Σx²/n − x̄²; standard deviation σ = √variance. Coding y = x + a changes the mean by a; y = kx multiplies the mean and standard deviation by k.

Example

Σx = 50, Σx² = 270, n = 10. Standard deviation?

Mean 5

270/10 − 25 = 2

Answer: √2 ≈ 1.41

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the square root.
  • Using Σx² ÷ n − mean (not mean²).
  • Thinking adding a constant changes the standard deviation.

faq.a: The population is split into groups and each group is sampled in proportion to its size.

faq.q: How does coding affect the standard deviation?
faq.a: Adding or subtracting a constant does not change it; multiplying by k multiplies it by k.

A set of marks has mean 35 and standard deviation 2. Every mark is increased by 10. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Adding the same amount for every value moves the mean by 10 but does not change the spread: mean 45, SD 2.

items.q: A set of marks has mean 75 and standard deviation 6. Every mark is increased by 10. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Adding the same amount for every value moves the mean by 10 but does not change the spread: mean 85, SD 6.

items.q: A set of marks has mean 79 and standard deviation 3. 4 is taken away from every mark. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Taking away the same amount for every value moves the mean by 4 but does not change the spread: mean 75, SD 3.

items.q: A data set has mean 25 and standard deviation 8. Every value is multiplied by 3. What is the new standard deviation?
items.e: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the spread by 3: 8 × 3 = 24.

items.q: Values with mean 25 and standard deviation 4 are each multiplied by 2 and then increased by 5. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Mean: 25 × 2 + 5 = 55. SD: only the multiplication matters, 4 × 2 = 8. mean 55, SD 8.
